info.title: MyF5 APIs — Observed Behaviour
info.description:
An OpenAPI description of the MyF5 APIs as they ACTUALLY behave, written
from live requests rather than from F5's published specification.

WHY THIS EXISTS

F5's published document (archived alongside this file) disagrees with the
running API on several points that each cost real debugging time. Where the
two differ, this file documents what the server did, and an
`x-observed-divergence` annotation records the disagreement. Every endpoint
carries `x-verified` stating when its behaviour was last confirmed, and
anything NOT exercised live is marked `x-verified: "UNVERIFIED"` so it is
never mistaken for fact.

SCOPE AND LIMITS

Only the GET paths and the rejection behaviour of POST /cases were exercised.
No case was created and no comment was posted, because both write visible
records to F5 Support. Those paths are modelled from their rejections and are
marked accordingly.

The API is rate limited to roughly 10 requests per minute per client; probing
beyond that returns 429 with a body unlike every other error shape here.

This file is maintained by hand. Treat it as a field report, not as a contract.

servers.description: Support APIs — Case Management. Requires the `k` usage key.
Downloads API (post 2026-10-02 ESDP cutover). Takes NO `k` parameter.
iHealth QKView API. Separate OAuth audience; no `k` parameter.

tags.name: downloads
tags.description: Software catalog and signed download links.

post.description:
Returns a bearer token for ONE resource server, named by `audience`.

A client is only authorized for audiences it holds a grant on. Requesting
the MyF5 audience with iHealth credentials fails with 403 "... is not
authorized to access resource server ...", so MyF5 and iHealth require
SEPARATE credential pairs — they are not interchangeable.

For the iHealth audience, `scope` must be OMITTED: that client is not
granted `ihealth` as a scope and access is conveyed by the audience alone.
post.x-verified: 2026-10-05 — used successfully for every live call in this document

audience.description: The resource server the token is for.

scope.description: Required for the MyF5 audience. MUST be omitted for the iHealth audience.

403.description: The client holds no grant on the requested audience.

get.description:
`type` is REQUIRED. Omitting it returns 400 "Missing type in the query params".

`status` does NOT widen the result set — it filters on comma-separated
metadata values such as "New,Solving". Use `type` to choose open vs closed.

post.description:
Opens a case.

Every case requires an ENTITLEMENT IDENTIFIER, but not the same one: which
field the API verifies depends on the product family.

  - BIG-IP and other hardware families -> serialNumber
  - NGINX, Aspen Mesh                  -> subscriptionId

Both are documented as optional in the published specification. Neither is.
The rejections differ by family, and the messages are misleading:

  - BIG-IP, no serialNumber   -> 400 "Serial Number,Product Family and Product
                                      are required to create Case."
  - NGINX,  no subscriptionId -> 403 "Unable to verify Subscription. Please make
                                      sure Subscription Number and Product
                                      Family vaules are provided." [sic]

The 400 names the same three fields regardless of which one is actually
missing, and is phrased for BIG-IP even when a different family was sent, so
it cannot be used to identify either the offending field or the right one.

The identifier is looked up, not merely checked for presence. A value that is
present but unrecognised returns 403 "The value entered is invalid or out of
Support." Reaching that means every OTHER field validated. Note this 403 is
about DATA, not credentials — the same status code the gateway uses for a bad
`k` key.

An invalid productFamily/product pair returns 400 "Valid Product Family and
Product are required to create Case.", which is a DIFFERENT message from the
missing-identifier 400 above.

Note on reasonForContact: "Pre Sales" is available to F5 Systems Engineers.
A customer account cannot open a presales case.
post.x-verified: 2026-10-05 — rejection behaviour only, probed across BIG-IP, NGINX and an invalid family. NO case was successfully created; a create needs a real in-support serial number or subscription. The 2xx response shape below is UNVERIFIED.
x-observed-divergence: Published spec marks serialNumber and subscriptionId optional; the live API requires one of them, chosen by product family.
Published schema's required list names `version`, while every example in the same document sends `productVersion`. `version` is what the API accepts.
The missing-identifier 400 is phrased for BIG-IP regardless of the productFamily submitted.

200.description: Case created. SHAPE UNVERIFIED — inferred from the envelope the other case endpoints use.

400.description: A required field is missing. The message names three fields whatever the actual omission was.

example.message: Serial Number,Product Family and Product are required to create Case.

403.description: A submitted VALUE was rejected — typically an unknown or out-of-support serial. Not a credentials failure.

example.message: The value entered is invalid or out of Support.  Please call F5 Technical Support if you require assistance.

parameters.name: caseNumber
parameters.description: Eight digits, no prefix, exactly as MyF5 displays it. A `C`-prefixed form appears in some older documentation and is not accepted.

get.description:
Returns a single case with contacts, account and the full email thread.

`data` is an ARRAY holding one element, not an object.
x-observed-divergence: `dateOpened` returns the PRIORITY string on this endpoint (observed: "4 - General Assistance"), while the list endpoint returns a real timestamp ("09/29/2026 17:59:42") for the same case. Server-side defect; prefer the list value.

patch.summary: Add a comment to a case
patch.description:
Appends a comment. The field is `comments`, PLURAL.

There is NO `/notes` sub-resource; an earlier client implementation posted to
one and silently did nothing useful.

The response reports failure in the BODY via `isError` as well as by status
code, so a 2xx alone does not mean the comment landed.
patch.x-verified: UNVERIFIED — exercising this writes a visible comment to a real support case. Modelled from the published spec and the shared envelope.

200.description: Comment accepted. Check `isError` before trusting it.

get.summary: Valid values for case creation (CURRENTLY BROKEN)
get.description:
The authoritative source of valid `productFamily`, `product`, `version`,
`priority`, `reasonForContact`, `preferredContactMethod` and `timezone`
values.

**OUTAGE — returns 500 for every request as of 2026-10-05.** The body reads
"Malformed JSON: Expected '{' at the beginning of object" even for a plain
GET carrying no body at all, and sending `{}` as a body does not change it.
The fault is server-side; there is no client-side workaround.

Consequence: the valid values for case creation CANNOT currently be
enumerated from the API. Copy them from an existing case instead.
get.x-verified: 2026-10-05 — 500 on every attempt, with and without a request body, after a full rate-limit cooldown

200.description: Metadata retrieved. NOT CURRENTLY OBSERVABLE — this endpoint is returning 500.

example.message: Malformed JSON: Expected '{' at the beginning of object

get.summary: Product family and product line catalog
get.description:
Note the DOUBLED `v1` in the path. It is not a typo: the leading segment is
the gateway's route version and the inner one is the API's. Omitting the
leading `/v1` returns 404 with an empty body.

This host takes NO `k` parameter — sending one is unnecessary. The host and
the dropped `k` both date from the 2026-10-02 ESDP cutover.
get.x-verified: 2026-10-05 — 200; the same path without the leading /v1 returned 404

404.description: Returned with an EMPTY body when the leading /v1 is omitted.

get.summary: Versions, containers and files for a product line
Signed regional CDN links for one file
get.x-verified: UNVERIFIED — not exercised in this session

get.description:
Returns ONLY ids — `{"id": ["26894783", ...]}` — not an array of objects.
Metadata lives on the per-QKView detail resource, so each id must be
fetched individually.

There is NO version segment in the path. The API versions by `Accept`
header; `/qkview-analyzer/api/v1/qkviews` returns 404.
get.x-verified: UNVERIFIED in this session — path and Accept behaviour recorded from earlier live testing (2026-10-02) documented in pkg/ihealth

post.description:
multipart/form-data. The file part is named `qkview`; `case_number` and
`description` are optional text fields. Attaching to a case requires the
case to already exist.
post.x-verified: UNVERIFIED — not exercised in this session

get.description:
The `+json` suffix on the Accept header is NOT optional. The bare
`application/vnd.f5.ihealth.api` returns 200 with an XML body, which then
fails to decode as JSON.
get.x-verified: UNVERIFIED in this session — Accept behaviour recorded from earlier live testing (2026-10-02)

KParam.name: k
KParam.description:
API usage key. A per-API-FAMILY constant published in F5's specification, not a per-user secret — Case, Downloads and Knowledge each have their own, and sending the wrong family's key returns 403.

Required on support.apis.f5.com. NOT used by the Downloads or iHealth hosts.

The published spec's own `rateLimitParam_Cases` example value is REJECTED by the live Case API with 400.

IHealthAccept.name: Accept
IHealthAccept.description: The `+json` suffix selects the JSON representation. Without it the API answers with XML.

RateLimited.description:
Rate limit exceeded — roughly 10 requests per minute per client.

The body does NOT use the standard envelope; it is a differently shaped
`errors` array emitted by the gateway rather than the application.

Envelope.description:
The standard response wrapper for Case Management.

`isError` is authoritative and independent of the HTTP status: a 2xx may
carry `isError: true`. Clients MUST check it before trusting `data`.

CaseSummary.description: A case as returned by the LIST endpoint.

dateOpened.description: Reliable on the list endpoint. See the note on CaseDetail.

allOf.description:
The detail view adds account, contacts and the email thread.

KNOWN DEFECT: `dateOpened` carries the priority string here, not a date.

caseOwnercontact.description: Note the lowercase `c` in `contact` — that is the wire spelling.

alternateContact.description: Shaped DIFFERENTLY from the owner contact: a split name and a phone number, and no preferred contact method.

CaseCreateRequest.description: The create payload, with the required list the SERVER enforces.

productFamily.description: From case metadata. Known-good values seen in F5's own examples: BIG-IP, NGINX, Aspen Mesh.

version.description: The published spec's examples call this `productVersion`; the schema and the API call it `version`.

serialNumber.description: Serial number, or the last 7 of a registration key. REQUIRED for BIG-IP and other hardware families despite the published spec marking it optional. Looked up server-side: an unknown or out-of-support value returns 403. NGINX and Aspen Mesh use subscriptionId instead.

priority.description: Per F5 article K2633. MyF5 may also display a "Low" option; K2633 states that is shown in error and is not valid.

reasonForContact.description: Observed live: "Pre Sales". F5's examples also use "General Problem".

timezone.description: Observed live on an existing case. Note F5's examples use a shorter bare-offset form such as "(GMT +10:00) GMT+10:00".

subscriptionId.description: REQUIRED for NGINX and Aspen Mesh, in place of serialNumber. Verified server-side: omitting it returns 403 "Unable to verify Subscription".
